title: Context Layer Reconciliation — proto journal
content:
Purpose:
This is my working notebook on a lightweight protocol for reconciling multiple context sources when serving generation requests. Goal is a small, composable API surface that lets clients and runtime exchange 'context fragments' (user prose, retrieval hits, KV cache entries, system overlays) and arrive at a deterministic merge for prompt construction, while preserving token accounting and privacy boundaries.

Motivating problems observed:
- Clients stitch retrievals + user message + session cache in ad-hoc ways; duplicates, stale embeddings, and conflicting system instructions slip into final prompt.
- Runtime caching (KV/prefix) can produce overlapping tokens with retrieval hits -> double-counting cost and unexpected behavior.
- Need for controlled evictions/TTL across layered caches when client and server both maintain versions.
- Migration from v1 context blobs (opaque JSON arrays) to richer typed fragments requires compatibility paths.

Design goals (non-exhaustive):
- Deterministic merge order: explicit priority ladder (system overlays > user message > session cache > retrievals by recency) but configurable per-route.
- Idempotent reconciliation: same inputs -> same merged output (important for caching and replay).
- Minimal bandwidth: allow clients to send fragment digests and let server fetch full fragment when cached/owned.
- Privacy boundary enforcement: fragments tagged as 'sensitive' cannot be persisted server-side unless customer opt-in.
- Token accounting: return a trace of token attribution per fragment for billing/debug.
- Backwards-compatible: allow server to accept v1 'blob' and treat it as a low-priority fragment.

High-level API idea: POST /v1/context/reconcile
Request (JSON sketch):
  {
    "request_id": "str",
    "route": "hosted.chat.complete",
    "fragments": [
      {"id":"f-1","type":"system","priority":100,"source":"client","content":"You are a helpful assistant.","sensitive":false,"digest":"sha256:..."},
      {"id":"f-2","type":"user_message","priority":90,"source":"client","content":"Summarize my notes:","sensitive":false},
      {"id":"f-3","type":"session_kv","priority":60,"source":"server","digest":"sha256:...","size_tokens":256},
      {"id":"f-4","type":"retrieval","priority":50,"source":"external","digest":"sha256:...","meta":{"score":"0.83","origin":"vectorstore_a"}}
    ],
    "config": {"max_tokens":2048,"merge_strategy":"priority-concat","dedupe_threshold":0.8,"return_attribution_trace":true}
  }

Notes on fields:
- id: client or server-assigned fragment identifier (opaque string).
- type: enum {system,user_message,session_kv,retrieval,tool_output,blob_v1}.
- priority: integer higher == earlier in final prompt unless strategy overrides it.
- digest: optional sha256 digest of stored fragment — server can check and reuse cached text.
- size_tokens: optional approximate token length when client knows it (helps planner).
- sensitive: boolean; if true, server must treat fragment as ephemeral and must not write to durable logs/caches without explicit permission.

Server-side behavior (sketch):
1) Validate request_id and auth.
2) Normalize fragments: if digest present and fragment not provided, attempt to lookup in local context-store; if not found and source==server -> reject.
3) For merge_strategy=="priority-concat": sort fragments by (priority desc, type tie-breaker), then apply dedupe: if similarity(contentA, contentB) >= dedupe_threshold -> keep higher priority fragment and add cross-ref.
4) Attribution trace: build array of {fragment_id, start_token_index, end_token_index, attributed_tokens}.
5) Apply size guard: if merged_tokens > config.max_tokens -> run eviction policy (lowest priority first) until under limit or return 413-like 'prompt too big' error depending on route SLO.
6) Return merged_prompt (string), token_attribution (list), and a reconciliation_summary with actions taken (evicted fragments, dedupe events, cached_hits).

Example response (sketch):
  {
    "merged_prompt": "<combined text>",
    "token_count": 1432,
    "attribution": [
      {"fragment_id":"f-1","start":0,"end":24,"tokens":24},
      {"fragment_id":"f-3","start":25,"end":300,"tokens":275}
    ],
    "actions": ["used_cached_f-3","deduped f-4 by f-3 (sim0.87)"]
  }

Config schema vignette (route-level config, kept compact):
  reconciliation:
    strategy: "priority-concat"  # priority-concat | temporal-merge | heuristic-token-binning
    global_max_tokens: 4096
    dedupe_threshold: 0.85
    attribution: true
    sensitive_handling: "ephemeral_only"  # ephemeral_only | allow_cache_with_consent
    eviction_policy: "priority_then_age"

Edge cases and rules I've been scribbling: 
- If two fragments are near-identical but both marked sensitive, prefer client-supplied fragment and never cache server-side.
- If client sends digest only and server fetch fails (evicted), return a 202 with action_needed: "REFETCH_FRAGMENT" and a short-lived presigned upload id so client can reupload content if it still wishes.
- For hybrid clients (mobile + server cache): implement a fragment lease header that encodes version and TTL so client can know if its local fragment can be trusted or should be revalidated.

ASCII flow diagram (rough):
  [client fragments] -> [reconcile API] -> {lookup cached fragment digests} -> [merge/dedupe/evict] -> [merged prompt] -> [model invoke]
                  
  with optional side-channel: if fragment fetch needed -> server returns REFETCH token -> client PUT /v1/context/upload/{token}

Migration notes from v1 blob (opaque list):
- v1 blobs will be treated as type blob_v1 with priority default 10. We will add a server-side extractor job that attempts to classify v1 blob into typed fragments (system/user/retrieval) and surface that as a hint but do not rewrite client-visible merged prompt until migration window ends.
- Add compatibility flag route_accepts_blob_v1=true on route config; default false for new routes.

Testing and evaluation checklist (quick):
- Determinism: replay same fragments, assert identical merged_prompt and attribution.
- Dedupe sensitivity: fuzz similarity threshold from 0.7..0.95 and check false merges on contrived near-duplicates.
- TTL/lease race: simulate client reusing evicted digest and assert server responds with REFETCH and not 500.
- Billing attribution: check token sums across fragments == merged token_count.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we expose an incremental/progressive reconciliation (streamed attribution) when a route needs low-latency start? (i.e., return first N tokens with attribution for early tokens while background compaction continues)
- How to represent structured tool outputs (json blobs) as fragments while still supporting token attribution? Use an adapter that serializes tool output as compact text + metadata link?
- UX for clients that want to 'pin' a fragment permanently server-side without sending full content every request; need secure upload + ownership model + opt-in billing.
- Garbage collection policy for server-owned fragments: soft-evict by age, hard-evict by size budget; expose GC hints to clients via lease TTL.

Quick TODO list (my immediate next steps):
- Draft a minimal GH PR with request/response shapes and a small reconcile service scaffold under serving-runtime/reconcile/ (prototype only).
- Add unit tests for deterministic ordering + dedupe.
- Chat with Maya about sensitive flag semantics and legal review for persistence.
- Sketch a lightweight lease token format (base64 of {id,expires,signature}) and a short spec for client libs.

Notes to self (brain dump):
- Keep the API opportunistic: server should be able to 'help' by returning cached content when digest known, but never surprise client by replacing client-sent content silently. Always include a summary of substitutions.
- Attribution trace will be super valuable in Console for debugging and cost breakdowns. Need to think about retention policy for attribution traces (PII risk?).

End of current entry. This doc is intentionally loose — primary aim is to have something to iterate on with Maya/Ravi and then move the canonical spec to Confluence once we converge on shapes.
